terra.problem: The text does not say whether Shechem had been sneaking around or mumbling.
The text does not say Jacob had nobody to talk to while he waited.
Jacob remaining silent does not establish that he did not go to the city gate.
The text says Jacob remained silent, not that he stayed put.
The text names grief and fury, but does not say the brothers were not scared.
Calling the proposed arrangement a happy ending is insensitive in the aftermath of Dinah's assault.
Shechem's delight and lack of hesitation do not establish that the condition did not make him angry.
Shechem's lack of hesitation does not establish that he felt no unease or had no second thoughts.
The text does not say that Hamor and Shechem had no idea what the brothers were planning.
The text does not say that Hamor and Shechem were unaware of the brothers' deceit.
Jacob's other sons appear earlier in the passage among the sons in the field and those who answer Hamor and Shechem.
The text does not state that Dinah was the reason Simeon and Levi came to the city.
